thread:
maria: Heads up — we're seeing ~20% lower prefix cache hit-rate in Private vs Hosted for the same demo traffic. Misses spike during startup/warmup.

alan: Any nearby releases that touched keying, warmup, or netstore clients? quick check pls.

maria: No deploys flagged in the window. I ran a flame from the runtime profiler — a lot of time spent waiting on netstore GETs and kernel fallback stalls.

ryan: Could be VPC egress + TLS handshake to customer netstore. Private clusters use encrypted NFS/gRPC tunnels in many cases. That adds RTT and sometimes CPU on TLS.

sophia: Correct — Private nets are typically customer-managed object stores (minio/s3 gateway) and sometimes NFS mounts in the air-gapped installs. Those return ~30ms vs ~5ms for our hosted redis netstore.

kevin: Also observed that when kernel selector falls back to the generic matmul path for specific seq_len distribution, token emission delays increase and we miss the prefetch window. Batching heuristics end up larger and then we get more misses.

debug-bot: autotriage: correlation(prefetch_misses, netstore_rtt)=0.71; correlation(batch_spike, miss_rate)=0.64; flagged as likely network-induced cache warmup regression.

maria: TL;DR: higher netstore latency in Private + occasional kernel fallback = slower warmup and lower early hit-rate. Need mitigations.

alan: Quick mitigation ideas: (1) in-process LRU for the most recent prefixes (small, lock-free) so first few requests hit regardless of netstore; (2) aggressive `prefetch-first-N` on cold sessions; (3) normalize cache keys to remove session-specific salts that increase key cardinality.

sophia: Note constraints for Private: cannot write to third-party shared caches; in-memory per-worker LRU is allowed. Also OSS-based netstores sometimes throttle bursts so prefetching needs pacing.

kevin: Suggest moving kernel selection earlier in the request path so we don't block kernel plan on netstore lookups. Precompute kernel plan from model+seq_len on arrival and reuse for the batch.

maria: I'll prototype a tiny per-worker LRU (capacity ~16k keys) + a `prefetch-first-8` flag gated behind an env var and a canary. Also add telemetry for: netstore RTT by env, kernel-fallback-counts, prefetch latency distribution, and per-prefix hit-rate over first 30 tokens.

alan: For Dedicated we could also consider an optional local memcached sidecar that the runtime can use if netstore RTT > 10ms. But we need ops buy-in for Dedicated infra.

ryan: For Private deployments with strict net restrictions we should add a fallback policy that prefers in-memory warm cache and degrades prefetch aggressiveness to avoid overloading customer stores.

ops-bot: Ticket INF-4823 created: "private-warmup-mitigation: per-worker LRU + telemetry + prefetch flag". Canaries scheduled on Dedicated then Private.

maria: I'll open the PR with benchmarks (microbench + end-to-end sim) and attach a deterministic replay of customer traces. Expect initial perf numbers: hit-rate (0-30 tokens) up from ~48% -> ~76% in sims with `prefetch-first-8` + LRU.

kevin: Also add a small perf test to ensure kernel selection change doesn't regress tail latency. We saw 95p increase previously when selector waited on netstore.

ryan: :thumbsup:

alan: Quick note: normalize keying to hashed(normalize_prompt(prompt) + model+version) — that trimmed ~12% key churn in earlier experiments. Avoid including request-scoped ids.

maria: Good call. I'll include normalization in the PR and bump the telemetry to show uniqueness rate pre/post.

sophia: If you need a Private testbed, we can spin up a sandbox with minio + simulated high-RTT link to mirror customer nets.

maria: Thanks — will coordinate.

debug-bot: Marking thread resolved when PR merges and canary hits 24h with no regressions.
